summary.text: A 50-year-old Caucasian woman had a nodular epithelioid cutaneous melanoma of the back resected in October 2010 and an axillary sentinel lymph node micrometastasis excised in January 2011, followed by radical axillary dissection with 0/18 involved nodes. In June 2011 she entered the CASVAC-0401 study and was assigned to the CSF-470 vaccine arm.

After 13 vaccinations over 2 years she developed a subcutaneous metastasis and bilateral lung nodules, and the subcutaneous metastasis was resected in June 2013. Its tumor carried BRAF V600E, FBXW7 S608T and CIC Δ374 mutations, with moderate-to-high mutational burden and an increase mainly of CD8, CD4 and CD20 lymphocytes relative to the primary tumor.

Blood lymphocyte, CD4, CD8 and NK counts rose during immunization, and TCRβ sequencing showed expansion of preexisting clones and appearance of new ones. About half of tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte clones were shared with blood two years after the protocol ended.

Vemurafenib 960 mg bid was started in December 2013 with a complete response within 3 months. She remained stable until December 2016, when lung, bone and brain metastases developed and holocraneal radiotherapy was given. At last contact in June 2017 she was alive.
